title: Why we built Autopilot: real application results with my resume
summary: What happened when Autopilot applied with my resume: early results from 115 applications, a tailoring before and after, and why some runs fail on purpose.
body_markdown:
As you might know, we have a new feature at Simplify called Autopilot. You pick a job, and Autopilot can tailor your resume, fill out the application and submit it for you.[Here's the Autopilot page](https://simplify.jobs/autopilot?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=why-we-built-autopilot&utm_content=intro-autopilot) .


We built Autopilot because applying for jobs gets repetitive fast. You find a role you like, then you're back to filling in your work history and tweaking the same resume. We already have[Copilot](https://simplify.jobs/copilot?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=why-we-built-autopilot&utm_content=intro-copilot) , which autofills applications for you, but it still needs you to sit there, find the job and double-check every detail. To make the whole thing more flexible, we built Autopilot and launched our[iOS app](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/simplify-ai-job-search/id6781911255?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) .


Autopilot Pros and Cons


From testing it with my own resume


Pros


- It saves a lot of time. You pick the jobs, and it handles the form-filling and resume tweaks.
- It gets the whole application ready for you, as long as it has what it needs.
- It uses your saved answers, so you're not typing the same stuff for every job.


Cons


- Not every job is supported yet.
- It won't make up answers. If you never mentioned something, Autopilot won't claim it for you, so some runsfail on purpose . That's how I'd want it to work.


I wanted to see how it does in a real job search, so I tested Autopilot myself with my actual resume. Here's the resume I used, and below is what happened. I hid my contact info so I don't get doxxed.


My original resume. It's super outdated, and the Stanford email on it has been deactivated.


## How I applied


I mostly used the Simplify iOS app for this, so I could queue jobs whenever and wherever. I'm pretty busy, so a lot of it happened on my commute. I'd tap Autopilot on a job and move on, then check back later to see what went through and how it answered the questions.


Autopilot in the Simplify iOS app.


## What happened when I applied with this resume


From August 31 through November 16, Autopilot applied to jobs for me with this resume. I went through the emails for **115 application or opportunity records** . Here's what I found so far:


How did I make this? It's the flow chart in Simplify's Job Tracker.Here's how to make one for your own search .


I found nine confirmed recruiter-call or live-interview invitations, six assessments with nothing later in the emails, and 35 rejections or closed opportunities without a confirmed interview invite. For the other 65 records, I couldn't find a later outcome.


Autopilot used my old Stanford email for these applications, and I don't use that email anymore. So if a recruiter reached out there, I probably missed it 😅 There could be a few more interview invites in there, so don't treat these numbers as final.


Also, an invite isn't the same as an interview, and no reply doesn't always mean a rejection. It's one batch, so I wouldn't read it as a typical interview rate.


## A real example: tailoring my resume to one job


Here's a real example of the tailoring step Autopilot runs before it applies. I picked a real Senior Software Engineer job. I'm leaving the company name out, but here are a few lines from the posting. I've highlighted the parts worth paying attention to:


From the job description


- Hands-on experience in full-stack development.
- owning problems end to end
- Designing and building robust, scalable solutions
- Playing an active role in architectural decisions and technical direction
- You'll work across cross-functional teams


I ran the same original resume against the same job description twice: once with **Keyword Distribution: Balanced** , and once with **Keyword Distribution: Maximum Match** , which I'm calling "Maxed" below. I kept **Measurable Results: Balanced** for both runs, so the keyword setting was the one I changed.


My settings for the Balanced run. For Maxed, I only switched Keyword distribution to Maximum Match.


I did this one in Resume Builder, so nothing got sent to the company.


## One bullet from my resume before and after


Here's my Simplify bullet, word for word, and what each setting did with it:


From my Simplify experience


Original


- Cofounded SaaS platform helping students find & apply to jobs in 1-click. Raised 3.2M+ from Craft Ventures, YCombinator, & high-profile angels. Hired & managed team of 10+ full-time engineers & developed core platform (full-stack).


Balanced · 1 keyword from the job description


- Co-founded and led end-to-end development of a full-stack SaaS platform enabling students to find and apply to jobs in one click; raised $3.2M+ from Craft Ventures, Y Combinator, and high-profile angels, and hired and managed 10+ full-time engineers.


Maxed · 5 keywords from the job description


- Co-founded and led a SaaS platform helping students find and apply to jobs in one click, exercising end-to-end ownership and full-stack development from product conception through production launch.
- Raised $3.2M+ from Craft Ventures, Y Combinator, and high-profile angels to fund product development and company growth.
- Hired and managed a team of 10+ full-time engineers, providing technical direction and team leadership while building scalable solutions through cross-functional collaboration; developed the core platform.


Highlighted keywords came from the job description. I left out the website line; the generated wording is unchanged.


Balanced kept it as one bullet and worked in one keyword from the job description, "end-to-end development." Maxed split it into three bullets and pulled in five: "end-to-end ownership," "full-stack development," "technical direction," "scalable solutions" and "cross-functional collaboration."


So if you use Maxed, check that it only claims things you actually did. Whichever setting I use, I read it next to the job description and make sure every phrase still sounds like something I did.


## When Autopilot fails on purpose


Sometimes an Autopilot run fails, and that's on purpose. If a required question isn't covered by your profile, resume or saved answers, Autopilot fails the run instead of making something up. I'd much rather it skip a job than send an answer I never gave.


Here's a real question from a recent run (not from my batch above), with the company left out:


- **"Do you have hands-on experience with automated API and UI testing"** : a required question with no answer, so the application didn't go through.


My own resume has the same gap. It says I built a full-stack platform, but it never mentions API or UI testing, and I wouldn't want Autopilot to guess. That's a detail I'd add myself.


If a run fails, add the missing info to your profile or saved answers, or finish that one yourself with[Copilot](https://simplify.jobs/copilot?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=why-we-built-autopilot&utm_content=stop-copilot) .[What to do when a run fails](https://help.simplify.jobs/en/help/articles/1787280-apply-to-a-job-with-autopilot?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=why-we-built-autopilot&utm_content=failed-application-questions) .


## Before you start


If you want to try Autopilot, check your profile, resume and tailoring settings first. It submits without a final review, so whatever's in there is what the employer gets. It's part of Simplify+.[Here's how the application flow works](https://help.simplify.jobs/en/help/articles/1787280-apply-to-a-job-with-autopilot?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=why-we-built-autopilot&utm_content=application-flow) .


Cool, want to see your own results?


[Sign up free](https://simplify.jobs/auth/register?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=why-we-built-autopilot&utm_content=button-1)


## Make a chart for your own search


Want to share how your search is going? First, make sure your application statuses are up to date. Here's where to find the chart on desktop:


1. Click **Tracker** in Simplify's top navigation to open[Job Tracker](https://simplify.jobs/tracker?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=why-we-built-autopilot&utm_content=job-tracker) .
2. Above your applications, click **Chart** , next to **Board** and **List** . This opens the **Application flow** chart.
3. Click **Save & Share** in the upper-right corner of the chart.
4. Give it a **Title** , add a description if you want, and choose whether to include demographic information. Then click **Save & Generate Link** and copy the share link. Anyone with that link can view the saved chart without a Simplify account.


For an image you can drop into a post or blog, open **Options** next to the Chart tab and choose **Export chart** to download a PNG. You'll also find **Saved charts** in that menu when you want to revisit a chart you've saved.[More on sharing your chart](https://help.simplify.jobs/en/help/articles/6486416-use-flow-chart-insights?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=why-we-built-autopilot&utm_content=share-progress) .
